mission.title: Disconnect
mission.description: Find out why the General's broadcasts have stopped, then shake off the System's attention.

npc.say:
It is said that he believes the program will cure his decaying flesh. If that is truly his condition, then he is to be pitied, non?
We here tend to take for granted our freedom from such frailties. This world grants us all the benefits of physical bodies, completely free of the weaknesses suffered by man. Any weaknesses we suffer here are entirely of our own making.
Don't worry; some get a bargain for theirs.

phase.briefing: The General seems to have thus far survived his trip toward the blackout zone 800 miles away--we can thank Zion's marvelously distracting bungle job of transferring their Commander Lock from EPN for some of that--but we haven't received his most recent update broadcast. This could mean that he's lying dead out there on some blackened, blasted rock--but let's not get our hopes up just yet. Before we start the party, you're going to go check with the commando squad in charge of relaying his transmissions, and see if they have any idea what's caused the delay.

enter.say:
Yeah, I heard something about that Commander Lock thing. EPN's been taking care of him in old Zion, and he finally got well enough to be shipped over to New Zion. So there was supposed to be some kind of hand-off of him between EPN and Zion hovercraft, but Veil and some Cypherites showed up, and then some Machine ships, and I think you can guess the rest. I still haven't heard who won or what happened to Lock, though.
Okay, the commando squad is... Uh... They're supposed to be in there, but I'm not getting any active readings here.

done.say: Ah, geez... That solves part of the mystery, anyway. Anything on their computer?
Uh-oh. Um... I'm gonna run quick a diagnostic our subnet that they were hooked into. Get back to you in a minute.

phase.briefing:
Well, {player}, you'll no doubt be pleased to hear that you've got the full attention of the System at the moment, and they aren't at all happy with you. Mm, no... I imagine they're a little riled up about the various hacks we've had to run on their systems to get the General past their Sentinel patrols. Of course, you can't be held responsible for more than just a very small, minor part of that...but consider this your fifteen minutes of fame.
Oh, come now, operative. I thought I could count on you to be useful for once in your life, and take the fall for this like a...well, whatever you call yourself. Now you want me to save you? Oh...fine, but I'm only doing this because it would look bad on my record if you were killed while on a mission for me.
Now, listen carefully. Go to the location I've marked for you, and find the room with the safe in it. It's shielded against scans. You should be perfectly fine in there.

enter.say: No signals in there... Maybe we ditched 'em.

objective.text: Find the room with the safe

done.say:
"Shielded against scans," huh? Riiight...
It's "safe" to say that your cover's blown. You'd better get out of there.

phase.briefing:
For crying out loud! I can't send you any Exile backup, operative--not with all those override programs still... Hm.
All right, don't say I never did anything for you. We've been tracking Halborn here and there, and it happens that I know of a spot where he's dropped one of his Accelerator programs. The Machines should give up the chase if you go hang out near that thing, since they won't want to get overridden.

enter.say: I'm reading a large override signal in there. Here's hoping this works...

done.say: There, you see? Now why don't you make yourself useful by cleaning up the Machines still hanging around outside the Accelerator's range.

phase.briefing:
You see? If you could follow my orders that promptly when your skin wasn't immediately at risk, you wouldn't have these problems in the first place.
Now that you've managed to delouse yourself, you can go report this escapade of yours yourself. And I'd rather you left my name out of it. It's embarrassing enough as it is...

enter.say:
Good thing for us Halborn's still playing irresponsibly with his override programs, I guess.
All right, look sharp, 'cause the boss is expecting you in there.

talk.say:
Hm. Yes, he has had his uses, but he still refuses to tell us anything about the program he wants, and now that he has removed the Oracle, he is without any impetuous that can be redirected to our own purposes. I think we can consider our business with him at an end.
Too bad... With his abilities, and my guidance, he had everything he needed to rise to a commanding position here.

done.say:
It is said that he believes the program will cure his decaying flesh. If that is truly his condition, then he is to be pitied, non?
We here tend to take for granted our freedom from such frailties. This world grants us all the benefits of physical bodies, completely free of the weaknesses suffered by man. Any weaknesses we suffer here are entirely of our own making.

Another of the many my husband has used and discarded over the centuries... Left an empty, purposeless husk--dead without knowing it.
It is the price we pay for trust, for being reckless in our attachments. It is what comes of insatiable desire--of wanting something so badly you are willing to sell your soul to get it.
Don't worry; some get a bargain for theirs.

mission.finish: Well, I said long ago that we shouldn't have had anything to do with Halborn. I knew this would happen. Now we'll probably have him hanging all over us, sobbing for us to take him back.
